{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Outsourcing Agreement (MSL / IBM)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer-side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Outsourcing Agreement, Statement of Work and attachments

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and confirm that the commercial core is strongly in our favour. Ownership of intellectual property in the Products vests in us by present and future assignment (§ 13.0), MSL gives a genuine third-party IP, compliance and warranty indemnity (§ 15.1), the warranty and remedy package (SOW § 19) sits at or above our preferred position, all audit rights run one way in our favour (§ 7.0), and there is no exclusivity, minimum-volume, MFN, non-compete or liquidated-damages exposure on us. Governing law and venue (New York) match our preferred position. Post-termination transition assistance is uncapped in duration in our favour (§ 5.2(a)(ii)).

Five terms fail the fallback and one expected protection is absent altogether:

1. **Limitation of liability (§ 15.3)** — critical. The cap is 3% of bill-of-materials value over the whole term (far below a 12-month fees measure) and there are **no carve-outs at all**, so MSL's § 15.1 indemnities, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct all sit inside that 3%. This is the priority redline.
2. **Assignment (§ 16.2)** — high. Flat mutual consent with no affiliate/successor carve-out for us and no reasonableness standard on the consent we must obtain. (§ 16.5 Sale or Merger is favourable to us and stays.)
3. **Termination for convenience (§ 4.0 / § 5.0)** — high. A fixed three-year term with cause-only exit; PO-level cancellation under SOW § 6.1 mitigates but is not an Agreement-level exit.
4. **Auto-renewal (§ 4.0; SOW § 2.0)** — medium. Non-renewal notice of six months (Base Agreement) and twelve months for six-month renewal periods (SOW), i.e. notice due before the renewal period begins.
5. **Non-solicitation (§ 9.0(f))** — medium. Scope and carve-outs are acceptable; duration is a redacted multi-year period exceeding our 12-month limit.
6. **Insurance** — missing. No CGL, professional liability or cyber cover anywhere; only narrow consigned-inventory and tooling property cover.

Several figures are redacted ([*]) in our copy and must be confirmed against the unredacted version (see Next steps).

---

## 2. Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 15.3 Limitations of Liability | Cap = 3% of bill-of-materials value over the term; no carve-outs. Mutuality satisfied. |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 15.1 Scope of MSL's Indemnity | Meets and substantially exceeds preferred; § 15.3(b) cap bites on it, addressed under LOL-CAP. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property | Ownership vests in us; exceeds preferred position. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 16.2 Assignment | No affiliate/successor carve-out for us; no reasonableness standard on our consent. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term (with § 5.0/5.1) | Fixed three-year term, cause-only exit; no mid-term convenience right. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 6.0 Purchase of Products | No exclusivity or requirements commitment on us. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6.1 Cancellation of Purchase Order | No LDs or early-termination fees on us; penalty mechanics run against MSL. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.0 Intellectual and Industrial Property | All grants run from us to MSL; ownership better than a licence. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 14.18 Restrictions and Limitations | No restriction on our business; use restrictions bind MSL. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | § 4.0 Term (and SOW § 2.0) | Six-month and twelve-month notice windows; no renewal price cap. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 9.0 Personnel | Duration "[*] years" from Effective Date exceeds 12 months; scope/carve-outs acceptable. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 7.0 Audit | All audit rights run in our favour; no reciprocal right against us. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 16.9 Governing Law | New York law and New York courts; no arbitration clause. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | Attachment 1 | Only MFN runs in our favour ("most favored customer" engineering pricing). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments/volume restrictions | Compliant | § 6.0 Purchase of Products | No take-or-pay; Appendix 2 accuracy true-up noted in diligence only. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination assistance and data return | Compliant | § 5.2 Rights Upon Termination | Uncapped exit assistance plus return obligations; return period redacted. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 Scope of Warranty | Express conformance/workmanship warranty, repair-replace-refund, epidemic failure; periods redacted. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 13.1 Consigned Products (only related cover) | No CGL, professional liability or cyber cover; fallback not met on any term. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 15.3(b) liability cap with no carve-outs.** MSL's indemnities, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct capped at 3% of bill-of-materials value. Position: reset the cap to the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable and US$1,000,000, and add an Excluded Claims sentence covering indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The clause stays mutual.
2. **§ 16.2 blanket assignment consent.** A prohibition on our assignment with no M&A carve-out is the walk-away case. Position: add an affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice plus a reasonableness standard, leaving MSL's restrictions and subcontracting notice duties intact; § 16.5 is confirmed unchanged for the avoidance of doubt.
3. **No termination for convenience during a three-year term.** Position: add a convenience right for us on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid amounts, preserving the §§ 5.2/5.3 wind-down and pricing bargain; confirm MSL has no convenience right.
4. **Non-renewal notice windows beyond 90 days (§ 4.0; SOW § 2.0).** Position: shorten notice to 30 days, align renewal periods at 12 months, add a 60-day renewal reminder and a lesser-of-CPI-or-3% uplift cap. Fallback: 60-day window with a 5% cap.
5. **Absence of any liability insurance.** MSL occupies our premises, handles our and our customers' inventory and accesses our I/T systems. Position: new § 16.22 requiring CGL, professional liability, cyber and workers' compensation cover at preferred limits, with certificates on request and existing consigned-inventory and tooling cover preserved. Fallback: E&O US$1M / cyber US$2M.

**Conditional:** the § 9.0(f) non-solicit becomes a walk-away item only if the redacted period exceeds 24 months. Our redline resets it to 12 months, with an 18-month landing zone available.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the five deviations plus the new insurance section, leading with § 15.3 and § 16.2 as the non-negotiables and holding the stated fallbacks in reserve.
2. **Obtain the unredacted figures** and confirm each against the playbook: the "[*] years" non-solicit period (§ 9.0(f)); the "[*] Days" confidential-information return period in § 5.2(a)(iii) (we revisit if materially longer than 30 days); the MSL Procured Parts and workmanship warranty periods and the § 16.19 survival cut-off (SOW § 19.1); and the Appendix 2 / § 13.0(f) requirements-accuracy percentages.
3. **Commercial sign-off** from the sourcing team on the Appendix 2 forecast-accuracy true-up percentages — noted as reliance-based reimbursement rather than take-or-pay, but the economics should be modelled before signature.
4. **Do not reopen** the compliant clauses. IP ownership (§ 13.0), the MSL indemnity (§ 15.1), warranty (SOW § 19), audit (§ 7.0), transition (§ 5.2) and the absence of exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume and LD exposure all run in our favour; the only sub-elements short of preferred wording (no affiliate extension on the indemnity, no machine-readable-format or all-systems deletion certification on data return, no express services or no-malicious-code warranty, non-exclusive venue wording) are noted for the record and not pursued.
5. **Confirm on close** that no side letter or purchase-order terms reintroduce exclusivity, minimum volumes or a reciprocal audit or non-solicit obligation on us."}
